note: The four inert tombstones: authenticated routes returning an unconditional HTTP 410 with no mutation. They are NOT public — calling them public would be a false statement about their auth stack — so they carry their own classification. THIS FILE IS NOT A LIST OF NAMES: TombstoneRouteBehaviourTest reads it and PINS THE SOURCE SHAPE of each closure (ReflectionFunction -> file + start/end line -> token stream with comments and whitespace dropped) against the `source` field below, AND proves the closure answers 410 with zero queries on EVERY configured database connection; RouteCoverageClassifier reads the same file. A planted branch, an extra call or a changed status code changes the normalised source and fails the pin — which is what makes the exemption earned rather than asserted (gate r2 B-3). To retire an entry, delete it here — the classifier then stops calling it a tombstone and the ratchet's growth direction fires, which is what 'a tombstone that stops returning 410 re-enters the uncovered count' means mechanically (spec 4.4.2, the paragraph at :1503). The `source` values are long (the retirement messages are long); the four below were DERIVED MECHANICALLY, not hand-written — token_get_all over each closure's own ReflectionFunction line range at `dev` 630afa86f, T_WHITESPACE/T_COMMENT/T_DOC_COMMENT dropped, tokens joined with one space — and each satisfies this test's own independent assertions (exactly one T_RETURN, body T_STRING identifiers exactly [response, json], no forbidden token, ends `, 410 ) ; }`). To re-derive after a deliberate change, run with TOMBSTONE_SOURCE_REGENERATE=1: it PRINTS/EMITS the four pins in the failure message and then DELIBERATELY FAILS, so a regeneration can never be a way to make this test green. It never writes this file.
